standfirst: A study workspace, not a product. Each campaign is one investigation scoped to one subject, and owns its glossary, plan, roadmap, and working material. Adding a second specimen doesn't start a new campaign — changing the subject does.

emptyState.title: No second campaign yet
emptyState.body: A new one starts by creating campaigns// with a CONTEXT.md and a campaign.json, then adding a row to CONTEXT-MAP.md and running node tools/build-campaign.mjs --all. That command writes the campaign's roadmap.html and worklog.html: both are generated and never hand-edited, and --all --check rejects a page that has drifted from its data. Copy this campaign's campaign.json structure, not its content — the thread menu is filed under the agent loop's five steps, and a different subject needs a different spine.

ownership.lede: The method outlives any one campaign, so it lives at the repo root. Anything that would be re-derived for a different subject lives inside the campaign.

rows.scope: That campaign's vocabulary — its output, not its input
The source of truth for the generated pages — registry, copy, and the log of findings. Hand-edited; everything the two pages show derives from it
Its map, board, and thread menu — generated from campaign.json, never hand-edited
What has actually happened — generated from the same file's log
Decisions scoped to that campaign (created lazily)
The method — decisions that outlive any one campaign
Issue tracker, triage labels, domain-doc rules
Shared instruments, e.g. the capture proxy and the page generator
This page's own copy — the standfirst, this table, and the terms below. campaigns/index.html is generated from it and every campaign's data
This map, plus the four shared method terms below

sharedLanguage.lede: Method vocabulary — the same in every campaign, so defined once in CONTEXT-MAP.md rather than in any one glossary.

terms.name: Campaign
terms.body: One investigation, scoped to one subject. It owns a glossary, a plan, a roadmap, and its working material. Avoid: study, project, investigation as a proper noun.

terms.name: Subject
terms.body: The category a campaign is ultimately about — never a particular artefact. A finding matters only insofar as it generalises to the subject.

terms.name: Specimen
terms.body: The particular artefact being dissected to learn about the subject. Chosen for being open and readable rather than for being representative.

terms.name: Transfer specimen
terms.body: A second artefact the vocabulary was not derived from, used to falsify it. Predictions are committed before it is examined, or the test proves nothing.
